cards.text: Last time, Ishmael struck down Gedaliah, the governor the king of Babylon had appointed, and now the people are afraid of the Chaldeans (Jer 41:2, 18). So Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, all the army commanders and all the people from the least to the greatest come to Jeremiah the prophet. They ask him to pray to the LORD for this remnant, because only a few of them are left.

cards.question: The commanders and the people want Jeremiah to pray for them. What do they want the LORD to tell them?

answers.text: The way to walk and what to do
How long Babylon will rule them
Who their next governor will be

cards.question: Jeremiah agrees to pray for the remnant, but says he'll only pass along the good news.

cards.text: Then the people go ALL in. They tell Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act upon every word that the LORD your God sends you to tell us."

cards.question: The people promise Jeremiah they'll obey the LORD's answer only if it's pleasant.

cards.text: After ten days, the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah. TEN DAYS of everybody staring at those three little dots in the group chat!
Jeremiah calls together Johanan, the commanders and all the people, from the least to the greatest. Then he gives them the answer from the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.question: The LORD's answer starts with an if. If the remnant does what, He'll build them up and not tear them down?

cards.text: Build up, not tear down. Plant, not uproot, and God even says He'll relent of the disaster He has brought on them.

cards.question: The LORD tells the remnant not to be ___ of the king of Babylon.
Why does the LORD say the remnant doesn't need to fear the king of Babylon?

answers.text: He is with them to save them
The king has gone back home
The king has made peace with them

cards.text: And it keeps getting BETTER. God says, "And I will show you compassion, and he will have compassion on you…"

cards.question: The LORD's promise to the remnant includes being restored to their own land.

cards.text: Staying in the land comes with all those promises. But then comes the second if: what if the remnant says, 'We will not stay in this land,' and disobeys the voice of the LORD?

cards.question: If the remnant won't stay in the land, where does the LORD say they might plan to go and live?
What do the people picture life in Egypt will be free of?

cards.text: No war, no ram's horn, no hunger for bread. Egypt sounds like a travel ad with a palm tree on it, but now comes the word of the LORD for the remnant of Judah, if they're determined to go there and live.

cards.question: The remnant fears the sword and dreads the famine. If they go to Egypt, what does the LORD say the sword and famine will do?

cards.text: The sword overtakes them there, and the famine follows on their heels. That's like moving across town to get away from a bill, and the bill BEATS YOU to the new address.

cards.question: The LORD says a few of those who go to live in Egypt will escape the disaster.

cards.text: Then God points back to Jerusalem. Just as His anger and wrath were poured out on the people living there, He says His wrath will be poured out on the remnant if they go to Egypt.

cards.question: If the remnant goes to Egypt, what does the LORD say they will never see again?

cards.text: Jeremiah makes it plain: "The LORD has told you, O remnant of Judah, 'Do not go to Egypt.' Know for sure that I have warned you today!"

cards.question: Jeremiah looks back at how the people sent him to pray and promised to do whatever the LORD said. What does he say they did?
Jeremiah tells the remnant they have obeyed the voice of the LORD in everything He sent him to tell them.

cards.text: Jeremiah says it straight: they have not obeyed the voice of the LORD. Friend, I promised my oven I'd stop opening the door to peek at the cookies, and I've peeked FOUR TIMES today, so I'm in no position to throw crumbs.

cards.question: Where does Jeremiah say the remnant will die by sword and famine and plague?

answers.text: In the place they want to live
On the road back to Mizpah

cards.text: So the remnant has God's answer in their hands, and now they have to choose. Hang on, friend, because this story's not done yet.

findings.problem: Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah and Ishmael appear for the first time in this lesson, but the card never says who they are. Jeremiah 42:1 lists Johanan and Jezaniah alongside the commanders, and Ishmael is named with no description at all.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 4 quotes the people promising to act on "every word" the LORD sends. That already rules out the answer that they'll obey only if the word is pleasant, so card 5's true-or-false question is given away before the baker answers it.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: In Jeremiah 42:14, life in Egypt free of war and hunger is something the remnant might say ("if you say..."). The question states it as a fact: "What do the people picture life in Egypt will be free of?" That drops the conditional framing the text gives it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card retells Jeremiah 42:16, which card 5 just asked and answered (the sword and famine follow them into Egypt). Apart from the joke, it doesn't move the passage forward.
This story card only restates card 12's answer, that they have not obeyed (Jeremiah 42:21), and then adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.
Six of the stop's eight choice cards are multiple choice, there are two true-or-false cards and there is no fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The final card is only the "story's not done" line plus a short wrap-up ("the remnant has God's answer in their hands"). It tells no content from Jeremiah 42:22, but it still cites Jeremiah 42:22.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the line saying the story isn't over (allowed when the last verse was asked on a choice card), what should its "verses" field cite: the last verse of the passage, the passage's whole range, or something else?
